judgments.reason: With coal still providing 3.4% of electricity in 2025, the statement that the phase-out is not complete is a reasonable interpretation of the data.
Gas generation at 79.7% in 2025 provides a factual basis for identifying reliance on gas as a primary system vulnerability.

requirements.evidence: Renewables rose by 15% between 2015 and 2025, reaching 16.9% of Israel's electricity.
requirements.reason: The report states both the 2025 renewables share (16.9%) and the change since 2015.

requirements.evidence: In 2025 coal still provided 14.3% of Israel's electricity, so the phase-out is far from complete.
requirements.reason: The report gives the 2025 status of coal, although it cites an incorrect share value.
The report does not include any comparison with Mediterranean peers.

requirements.evidence: Total generation increased from 64.2 TWh to 82.1 TWh over the decade.
requirements.reason: The report explicitly provides the electricity generation growth between 2015 and 2025.

requirements.evidence: Israel's reliance on gas (79.7% of generation in 2025) is the main vulnerability: any disruption to gas supply would hit most of the power system.
requirements.reason: The report identifies a key risk regarding gas supply disruption, grounded in the 2025 gas share data.
